messages:
Anya: Heads-up — after yesterday's int4 rollout on the 70B baseline we see a 6–12% latency tail increase on long-context chat loads. Root cause WIP but initial traces point at kernel-selection churn + KV cache warmup.

Mike: Can you paste the perf traces? is it batches or per-token? :thinking: 

Anya: short dump — spikes happen ~200–800 tokens in when histories are long. Not single-token jitter, it's sustained 50–200ms tail on p95 for some requests.

Priya: Interesting. Did quant calibration change layer ordering or slow down KV lookups? We had a change that selectively quantized projection matrices but left q/k/v FP32 in a few layers.

Anya: yes — per-layer partial quant: embeddings & lm_head excluded, some mid-layers left fp16, head layers int4. Kernel selector keeps flipping between fp8-attn kernels and int4-ff kernels each step.

Leo: That kernel-hop can cause micro-scheduling stalls. Selector heuristics prefer fastest kernel per-layer + batch shape. Mixed per-layer types -> scheduling overhead + different launch patterns -> context-switch cost.

Anya: Also noticed KV memory layout flip when we hit an int4-attn layer: we convert cached KV to packed int4 layout for that layer, then convert back -> extra memcpy + quant/dequant every few layers.

infra-bot: deploy:runtime-2026-11-20 applied to canary (3 nodes) — observing increased cpu on runtime-worker.

Mike: Do we have profiler samples? device timelines or host scheduler traces?

Anya: Attached snippets:
```
# device timeline top
kernel_launch: fp8_attn_kernel (0.9ms)
kernel_launch: int4_ff_kernel (1.2ms)
memcpy: quant_pack (2.4ms)
memcpy: dequant_unpack (1.8ms)
# host: scheduler wait 0.4ms per layer switch
```

Priya: Those memcpys explain the tail. Quant pack/unpack every few layers will kill throughput for long sequences.

Leo: Two mitigations:
1) enforce contiguous quantization segments: avoid switching layout mid-seq (quantize contiguous blocks of layers only)
2) lazy KV conversion: keep KV in fp16 warm cache and only convert on first use for pure-int layers, then reuse packed layout for subsequent tokens

Mike: Also consider kernel-selection hysteresis: if selector flips back/forth, pin to previous kernel for N tokens unless perf delta large.

Anya: Calibration note: the new per-layer calibration introduced per-weight scaling tables read during packing causing cacheline misses.

Priya: Can we move calibration tables to GPU and fuse pack+scale into a device kernel to avoid host roundtrip?

Leo: Repro plan:
- long-context replay (1k tokens) with partial-quant config on canary
- profile device timeline + host scheduler
- variant A: contiguous-quant-blocks
- variant B: hysteresis pinning
- variant C: fused pack-on-device

Anya: Spinning jobs now; will post numbers in ~2h. For immediate safety we rolled back the per-layer calib patch on canary.

infra-bot: rollback:runtime-calib-2026-11-19 triggered on canary cluster

Mike: If fused pack looks good, add a kernel-selection rule to prefer fused path when mixed precision crosses layer boundary.

Priya: Keep embeddings/lm_head exclusion — helps final-token quality.

Leo: I'll add selector-flips/sec metric to console so we can quantify flipping.

Mike: +1 on selector-flips. Also instrument kv-conversion-count.

Anya: thanks all — ping me for access. :coffee:
